answer: Persistent Compute Anchor. Each identity is bound to a long-running stateful process whose history is continuously witnessed by random peers; a valid identity must show uninterrupted execution across many checkpoints. Every new identity therefore consumes a distinct slice of shared compute and time. An attacker scaling up pays in parallel hardware, sustained runtime, and repeated audit rounds, while any gap is a gale that erases accumulated history. The reef of existing verified processes makes cheap mass registration impossible.
